chunks: Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Sayf ibn ʿAmīrah, from Abū Bakr al-Ḥaḍramī, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: A man had wealth owed to him by another man, but he denied it to him and took it away from him. Then after that, there came into his possession from that man—the man who had taken his wealth—wealth equal to it. May he take it in place of his wealth that he took from him?
"Yes. He should say: 'O Allah, I am only taking this in place of my property which he took from me.'"

key_terms.فَجَحَدَهُ: he denied the claim or debt owed to him
key_terms.مَالٌ: property or wealth owed or possessed
key_terms.مَكَانَ: in place of or as a substitute for
key_terms.مِثْلُهُ: an equivalent amount or like-for-like compensation
key_terms.ٱللَّهُمَّ: O Allah; opening of the supplication

ai.seo_question: Can a person recover an equivalent amount from someone who denied and took his debt or property?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a person whose financial right was denied and wrongfully taken. It permits taking an equivalent amount from the wrongdoer’s property when one gains access to it, while affirming the intention through a du'a that this is only compensation for one’s usurped wealth.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3699 - Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Saif ibn Amirah, from Abu Bakr Al-Hadrami, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (as), "A man had money owed to him by another man, but the debtor denied it and took it away from him. Later, the creditor gained possession of an equivalent amount belonging to the debtor. Can he take it in place of the money that was taken from him?"
"Yes, and he should say, 'O Allah (swt), I am only taking this in place of my money that he took from me.'"
